newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares steam ahead in Beirut weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares steam ahead in Beirut weekly trade.

text.p: Bank stocks moved ahead on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ending on Friday but turnover was slightly down and brokers said investors were waiting for second quarter results before jumping in strongly.
"People are waiting for the second quarter results," said one trader. "There was a good volume traded on all the stocks."

Solidere A and B shares both rose after weeks of lingering close to their all-time lows. The LIBX bank index rose 3.20 percent on the week to 163.82. The LISPI general index rose 1.36 percent, hitting 89.44 and the BLOM general index rose 2.35 percent to 964.80.
Market turnover fell slightly to 895,941 shares from 917,885 shares. The value of traded shares dropped to $9,091,750 from $12,590,502 but one broker sounded a note of optimism.
"It's not a matter of fundamentals any more. There is so much liquidity. The market could still go up in the coming months," he said.
Banque Audi, considered by many brokers the market's blue chip stock, rose to $25.375 from $24.875 a week earlier. The share touched a high of $26 on Tuesday before falling back.
"Audi is expected to rise further. People are really bullish about Audi," said another trader.
Other market leaders also made gains.
Banque Libanaise pour Le Commerce climbed to $19.625 from $18.5, setting new highs on four straight days.
"BLC is rising because it is still the most undervalued among bank shares," said Alain Balian, deputy manager at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest.
Bank of Beirut rose to $4.0 from $3.938.
"Preliminary estimates of BOB's mid-year earnings are very positive. The bank is expected to go beyond expectations. We have witnessed an increase in demand on the share," said a trader.
Solidere A and B both rose to $11.0 from $10.25 and $10.75 respectively as robust demand outstripped supply.
Of the four industrial firms listed, pipemaker Eternit fell to $1.78125 from $1.875 with only 150 shares changing hands.
Ciments Libanais was flat at $1.28125 amid a fair amount of trade. There was no trade in either tilemaker Uniceramic or Ciment Blancs.
